subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph, what does the gradient of the straight (linear) region represent?
questions.explain: For the linear region, F = ke, so the gradient (force ÷ extension) is the spring constant k. The area under the line gives the elastic potential energy stored.

questions.q: More distant galaxies generally show a:
options: Greater red-shift, meaning they move away faster
questions.explain: More distant galaxies have greater red-shifts, indicating they are receding faster.

questions.q: What provides the centripetal force that keeps a planet in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explain: Gravitational attraction between the Sun and planet provides the centripetal force for the orbit.

questions.q: Which of these correctly describes our solar system?
options: One star, eight planets, plus dwarf planets and moons
Only the Sun and the Earth
questions.explain: Our solar system contains one star (the Sun), eight planets, several dwarf planets (such as Pluto) and many moons (natural satellites).

questions.q: Heating a substance without changing its state increases its internal energy. Specifically, it increases the particles'...
options: kinetic energy, so the temperature rises
potential energy only, so temperature stays constant
questions.explain: When heating raises temperature (no state change), the energy increases the particles' kinetic energy, so they move faster and the temperature rises.

questions.q: What do all waves transfer from one place to another?
questions.explain: Waves transfer energy (and information) without transferring matter. The particles or fields oscillate about a fixed position; they are not carried along with the wave.

questions.q: How does the red-shift of a galaxy relate to its distance from Earth?
options: More distant galaxies have a smaller red-shift
Red-shift is the same for all galaxies
More distant galaxies have a larger red-shift, showing they recede faster
questions.explain: The more distant a galaxy, the greater its red-shift, meaning it is moving away faster. This is evidence that the whole universe is expanding.

questions.q: What is a beta (β⁻) particle?
options: A proton ejected from the nucleus
A high-speed electron emitted from the nucleus
questions.explain: A beta-minus particle is a high-speed electron emitted from the nucleus when a neutron changes into a proton. An alpha particle is a helium nucleus; gamma is an EM wave.

questions.q: If a satellite moves to a higher orbit (larger radius), to stay in a stable orbit it must travel:
questions.explain: At a larger orbital radius the gravitational force is weaker, so a slower orbital speed is needed for a stable orbit.

questions.q: A low polar orbit satellite is useful for:
options: Live television broadcasting to one fixed dish
Scanning the whole surface of the Earth, e.g. for weather and imaging
questions.explain: Low polar orbiting satellites pass over different parts of the Earth as it rotates, ideal for imaging and weather monitoring.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable as it is replenished and will not run out. Coal, natural gas and nuclear fuel are finite (non-renewable) resources.

questions.q: Which method would best reduce unwanted energy transfers between a machine's moving parts?
questions.explain: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, reducing energy dissipated to the thermal store. Insulation and streamlining are other valid methods of reducing unwanted transfers.

questions.q: A stretched elastic band stores energy in which store?
questions.explain: Stretching or compressing a spring or band stores energy in the elastic potential store.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between energy and power?
options: Power is energy stored; energy is the rate of transfer
Power is the rate at which energy is transferred
Energy and power are the same quantity
Energy is measured in watts; power in joules
questions.explain: Power is the energy transferred per second (P = E/t), measured in watts; energy is measured in joules. Confusing the two is a common error.

questions.q: Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays can be dangerous to living cells mainly because they are:
options: Ionising, so they can damage cells and DNA and cause cancer
Too slow to escape the body
questions.explain: UV, X-rays and gamma rays carry high energy and are ionising. They can damage cells and mutate DNA, increasing the risk of cancer; radiation dose is measured in sieverts (Sv).

questions.q: Which particles are found inside the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral). Electrons (negative) orbit the nucleus in energy levels (shells).

questions.q: For an object in a stable circular orbit, the centripetal force is directed:
questions.explain: The centripetal force always acts towards the centre of the orbit.

questions.q: What process releases energy in the core of a star like the Sun?
options: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
questions.explain: Stars release energy by fusing hydrogen nuclei into helium.

questions.q: A massive star much bigger than the Sun can end its life as a:
options: Nebula that never forms a star
Neutron star or black hole after a supernova
questions.explain: A massive star explodes as a supernova, leaving behind a neutron star or, if massive enough, a black hole.

questions.q: The cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation is considered:
options: Evidence for the Big Bang theory
Proof that the universe is shrinking
questions.explain: The CMB is faint microwave radiation from across the sky, regarded as strong evidence for the Big Bang.

questions.q: What is the first stage in the formation of a star?
options: A cloud of gas and dust called a nebula
questions.explain: Stars form from a nebula, a cloud of gas and dust pulled together by gravity.

questions.q: Elements heavier than iron are mainly formed:
options: During the explosion of a supernova
In the cores of small stars
questions.explain: The huge energies of a supernova explosion create and distribute elements heavier than iron.
